# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 69 (Bu-Vb Sk69)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk69
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 69
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting on a low seat
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-sk69
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Sekhiya 69 (*Nīcāsana*) is a Vinaya training rule belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga that prohibits a monastic from teaching the Dhamma while seated on a low seat to a listener who is seated on a higher seat and is not sick, as such a posture indicates disrespect toward the teaching [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. The background story framing the formulation of this rule incorporates the narrative of the *Chavaka-jātaka* (Ja 309; Vin IV 203–204), in which the Bodhisatta was born as an outcaste (low-caste man) who taught a mantra to a king seated above him; unlike standard Jātakas with explicit identifications, the Bodhisatta's identity as the outcaste is merely implied at the close of the account when the Buddha reflects that even in the past, teaching from a lower seat was distasteful to him [Appleton 2010; SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is shared virtually universally across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing in both Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Theravāda, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes narrative and verse parallels with Jātaka stories, including Ja 309 (*Chavakajātaka*), Ja 310 (*Seyyajātaka*), Ja 433 (*Lomasakassapajātaka*), and Ja 287 (*Lābhagarahajātaka*) [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus registers 363 internal Pali matches across 89 texts, reflecting shared Vinaya formulary, disciplinary sequences, and narrative phrasing with Sekhiya 57, Sekhiya 75, several Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 2 and Pc 21), Khandhaka sections (Kd 6, Kd 11, Kd 12), and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
